- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon; apply 1–2% upward bias for first 5–7 days of forecast.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings >0.25), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before next prediction.
- If sentiment is rising steadily (e.g., 0.3→0.7 over 5 days), model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast slope by 0.1–0.3 per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For long-term (15+ day) forecasts, model tends to underestimate; apply 1–3% upward bias if sentiment remains above 0.5 for 3+ consecutive days.
